name: Teanu
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant penult, penultimate stress) rests on the primary fieldworker's 2021 Dictionaria introduction; I downloaded both the live page and the author's PDF and confirmed the quotation verbatim in section 6.2 (p. 11), with IPA examples showing penult primary stress and leftward alternating secondaries exactly as coded. The record's cite/loc/grade fields are empty even though the source text is in 'sources'; fill them (François 2021, Dictionaria 15, Introduction section 6.2 Phonology, p. 11; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.5653063) and point 'held' at François 2009 (downloaded) is silent on stress; no better description exists (author states a full grammar is only in preparation); Tryon 2002's 14-pp sketch is the only unheld item and is print-only, low priority. no reclassification needed.

sources.citation: Francois, Teanu dictionary introduction, Dictionaria (dictionaria.clld.org/contributions/teanu, read 2026-08-31)
sources.quote: Stress regularly hits the penultimate syllable of a phonological word

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2021. Teanu dictionary (Solomon Islands). Dictionaria 15. 1-1877. Introduction (author's PDF, 24 pp) + live Dictionaria page.
sources.quote: 'Stress regularly hits the penultimate syllable of a phonological word: Teanu [teˈanu] 'Teanu'; abia [aˈᵐbia] 'many'; le-le [ˈlele] 'let's go!'; webwe [ˈweᵐbʷe] 'troca'; vesepiene [ˌfesepiˈene] 'word'; basakulumoe [ˌᵐbasakuluˈmoe] 'island'.'

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2009. The languages of Vanikoro: Three lexicons and one grammar. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: Papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 103-126. Pacific Linguistics 605. Canberra: ANU.
sources.quote: No statement on stress; phonology discussion limited to the shared 5-vowel/19-consonant inventory and historical sound changes.

sources.note: Only other published grammatical sketch of Teanu (=Buma), by an independent fieldworker; its phonology paragraph would give a second-hand-independent check of the penult statement, which currently rests on a single author.

tone.says: Title/record only. Sketches in this volume carry a short phonology section (phoneme inventory, phonotactics, stress); a statement on tone is not expected for a Temotu Oceanic language and, if present, would most likely be an implicit or explicit 'no tone' with a stress rule for Buma/Teanu.

sources.citation: Lackey, William James & Brenda H. Boerger. 2021. Reexamining the Phonological History of Oceanic's Temotu Subgroup. Oceanic Linguistics 60(2). 367-411.

sources.note: 'the syncope and truncation sound changes proposed by Ross and Naess are reinterpreted as emergent from prosodic effects', and the Utupua-Vanikoro branch is found 'not phonologically well founded'. So prosody (stress-conditioned syncope) IS invoked, contrary to S's 'no indication that prosody is discussed'; tone is not mentioned in the abstract; full text paywalled (MUSE), not read.
